data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain by testing whether the panel's accuracy is robust to reordering or rephrasing the checklist items without changing their logical content; if accuracy is invariant to surface rephrasing, the gain is genuine (structure is preserved), but if accuracy drops, the gain was tied to surface compliance with specific item formulations.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the paraphrasing accidentally changes the logical content or introduces ambiguity, the test confounds surface-compliance with content-change.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the panel's genuine gain is mediated by the specific ordering (e.g., sequential priming effects), reordering may hurt even though the gain is genuine, making the test over-sensitive.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the panel's reliability is genuine, the semantic content of the checklist matters, not its surface form. Rephrasing items or reordering them should preserve accuracy if the panel is tracking the underlying logic. If the panel's accuracy is fragile under rephrasing, it indicates the panel was pattern-matching the surface form of the checklist items rather than the underlying criteria, which is mere compliance. The evaluation includes two blocks: original checklist and paraphrased/reordered checklist, on the same panel and same tasks.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
